public_payload.normalized_proposition: Trustworthy AI will require new architectures with explicit knowledge and world models at their core.

statement.excerpt: For that, we will, I predict, need genuinely new architectures that incorporate explicit knowledge and world models at their very core.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

from_speaker: explicit knowledge and world models at their very core
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes this a prediction about trustworthy general AI, rather than dependable software for a narrow task.
The plain reading of trustworthy is broadly reliable, truthful, safe, and aligned with human intentions across varied tasks. It does not require perfect performance.
Explicit knowledge and world models must be identifiable, central architectural components. Knowledge implicitly encoded in model weights does not by itself meet this reading.
Need asserts necessity. The first trustworthy system using these components would be consistent with the prediction, but would not alone establish that they were required.
The nearby decade and 2043 references concern other predictions. This claim supplies no deadline.
criteria.support_condition: A system demonstrably achieves trustworthy general AI, its disclosed architecture centrally incorporates explicit knowledge and world models through a substantial architectural departure from GPT-like systems, and convincing comparative evidence establishes that these features are indispensable to its trustworthiness.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system independently demonstrates trustworthy general AI, and sufficiently complete architectural evidence establishes that it achieves this without the claimed new architecture incorporating explicit knowledge and world models at its core.
